requirements.description:
1 4.9.8 — Hormone Rhythm separation and educational personalization

Preserve the existing Hormone Rhythm educational visualization, including its artwork, design, and educational explanations.
The app must distinguish between:
    • Hormone Rhythm: Typical, research-grounded educational patterns of hormonal changes throughout the menstrual cycle.
    • My Measurements: Actual hormone values entered by the user, including their units, dates, and relevant testing information.
    • Adjusted Rhythm: An optional educational visualization informed by the user’s recorded hormone measurements.
Educational personalization requirements:
   1. Use Fruitfolio’s existing Research Library and Approved Source Library exclusively to support all educational adjustments.
   2. Allow users to opt into adjusting Hormone Rhythm based on their recorded hormone measurements.
   3. Preserve scientifically established relationships between hormones and menstrual-cycle physiology.
   4. Only adjust educational curves when sufficient research and measurement context support a scientifically defensible illustration.
   5. Use recorded measurements as reference points without assuming unmeasured hormone concentrations.
   6. Never fabricate, interpolate, or predict the user’s actual hormone levels.
   7. Never present adjusted educational curves as the user’s measured hormonal profile.
   8. Clearly distinguish educational curves from actual measurements through labels, legends, and visual styling.
   9. Preserve the original Hormone Rhythm and allow users to restore it at any time.
  10. Never modify or overwrite measurements stored in My Measurements.
  11. Do not automatically adjust cycle-prediction confidence based on entered hormone measurements.
  12. Do not use adjusted educational curves to diagnose conditions, confirm ovulation, determine fertility, or recommend treatment.
  13. Do not automatically share hormone measurements with Ask AI.
  14. Ensure all educational explanations and adjustments follow Fruitfolio’s existing research-grounding and citation requirements.
  15. If insufficient research or measurement context exists, retain the original educational visualization and explain why personalization is unavailable.
Required disclosure when educational adjustments are applied:
your hormone rhythm <3
this educational illustration has been adjusted using your recorded hormone information. the curves show possible hormonal patterns, not your measured hormone levels. actual hormone concentrations may differ.
The disclosure must remain accessible whenever an adjusted visualization is displayed.
Insufficient-information message:
a little note! ☆
your measurement has been saved, but there isn’t enough information to adjust this illustration reliably. you can still explore the typical hormone rhythm and view your actual result in my measurements.
Visualization behavior:
    • Default Hormone Rhythm: Display the original research-grounded educational visualization.
    • Adjusted Rhythm: Display research-supported educational adjustments informed by recorded measurements, with clear labeling and disclosure.
    • My Measurements: Display only actual user-entered measurements, preserving their original values, units, and dates.
Measurement-history graphs must contain only recorded measurements. Do not interpolate missing values or display predicted laboratory results.
All three modes must follow Fruitfolio’s existing visual design, accessibility, privacy, localization, and medical-safety requirements.
Acceptance criteria:
The feature passes only when the original Hormone Rhythm remains intact, educational personalization is optional and clearly disclosed, actual measurements remain separate and unchanged, unsupported adjustments are prevented, and cycle-prediction confidence is unaffected by hormone measurements.

requirements.description: PROMPT 1B ADDITION — ASK CONTINUOUS PAPER, SCROLLING, AND SESSION-ONLY HISTORY (2026-10-16; binding requirement). Preserve all existing Ask functionality, Research Library retrieval, citations, Canonical Voice, Semantic Stylization, typing ASMR controls, suggested questions, and the founder-authored paper/art composition. The user must be able to scroll vertically through their previous questions and complete answers within the current Ask session, including long replies, without losing access to earlier text. Present the Ask conversation as one continuous, visually infinite paper journal: the paper grows downward with content and/or uses a seamless repeatable paper treatment so there is no visible bottom edge, hard height cap, clipping, sideways expansion, or forced truncation. Maintain stable, centered paper width on every supported iPhone size, orientation, localization, and Dynamic Type size; center the readable text column horizontally within the actual paper bounds, with responsive interior padding and a text-safe region that never collides with the fruit artwork. Text must wrap and expand vertically; do not shrink text to force it to fit. The user can scroll both up and down to revisit any question or answer from the active session; when a new answer streams in, auto-follow only while the user remains near the bottom, and never yank the viewport away when they are reading older content. Preserve selection, citation links, and accessibility reading order while scrolling.

requirements.description: The canonical orange slice, orange glow, and pear slice are anchored to their approved positions relative to the paper composition, not to absolute device-screen pixels. They move naturally with the paper when the user scrolls (they are not fixed viewport overlays); their relative arrangement, size hierarchy, and spacing stay visually stable and responsive. Preserve the existing opening-state requirement that the orange is centered with the other two balanced on either side; the fruit must not obscure any question, answer, citation, button, or editable control. Treat the fruit composition as part of the paper layout, with a reserved decoration-safe area. Do not duplicate the three fruit images on every appended paper segment, stretch their native art, or create floating fruit over the text. On an infinitely growing paper, the decorations remain at their designated composition anchor and travel through the scroll view with it. Maintain paper centering and art-to-paper alignment based on measured runtime geometry rather than hardcoded offsets.

requirements.description: Ask conversation lifetime is strictly session-only unless the user explicitly saves content to a Guide. During the active Ask visit, keep the visible question/answer history available for scrolling. When the user exits Ask (navigates away, closes its view, ends the visit, or restarts the app), clear that unsaved Ask conversation and any unsaved draft text; the next entry opens a blank-slate paper with the original three fruit decorations, question-entry controls, and recommended questions. Do not silently restore prior Ask transcripts through app state restoration, account sync, background persistence, search history, or analytics. A temporary in-memory session buffer is permitted for rendering while Ask is open; clear it on exit. Saving to a Guide is the sole durable save action for Ask-generated content: explicitly selected questions/answers, their supporting citations, and necessary attribution can persist within the user’s chosen Guide using the existing Guide Builder flow, and must remain accessible from that Guide even after the Ask session is cleared. Merely receiving an answer, scrolling it, selecting text, or using an unsaved bookmark-like UI must not persist the transcript. A successful save should give clear confirmation; canceling or failing to save must not create a persistent copy. Do not delete independently saved Guide content when Ask is cleared. Retain privacy, local-data boundaries, and the ability to discard sensitive text; if a user explicitly navigates to save, preserve only the selected save payload until that operation resolves. Test short/long/multiple answers, small/large screens, accessibility text sizes, scroll-to-history, leaving/reopening, app relaunch, canceled save, and successful Guide save.

Use body_heart for cardiovascular/heart history; body_thyroid for thyroid/endocrine history; body_liver for liver/metabolic history; body_stomach for stomach/digestive history; body_gut_microbiome for gastrointestinal/gut or microbiome history; body_kidneys for kidney/urinary history; body_skin for dermatologic/skin history; body_bone for bone/skeletal history; and body_muscle for muscular/musculoskeletal history, with each opening an optional “anything you want Fruitfolio to know?” free-text field. Include all canonical Genetics artwork as optional family/genetic/biological-context entry points: genetics_dna for known genetic conditions, variants, or other DNA/genetic information the user wants to record; genetics_chromosome for known chromosomal conditions/findings; genetics_mitochondrion for known mitochondrial conditions/findings; genetics_cell and genetics_cells for other known cellular/medical history that does not fit a more specific category; genetics_rna for known RNA-related genetic/molecular findings; genetics_protein for known protein-related genetic/molecular findings; genetics_receptor for known receptor-related conditions/findings; and genetics_nucleus as an other genetics/genomics information entry point. These genetics fields must remain optional and may store only information the user explicitly supplies; Fruitfolio must never infer a genotype, mutation, carrier status, inheritance pattern, disease risk, or diagnosis from another answer. Use symptom_medication for an optional medication-history field where users may enter medications and any details they choose; retain the separate structured hormonal-birth-control/fertility-medication questions for prediction logic. Use lab_agar_plate, lab_centrifuge, lab_microscope, lab_collection_swab, lab_microcentrifuge_tube, lab_test_tube, lab_transfer_pipette, and lab_specimen_cup as specific optional laboratory/testing-history entry points only when their depicted testing/sample concept legitimately applies—for example, cultures/microbiology, microscopy, swab/sample collection, specimen collection, or user-entered laboratory/testing information—and never imply that a particular laboratory technique was performed merely because the user reports having a test; provide an other labs/testing field so users are never forced into an inaccurate artwork category. Reproductive artwork may also provide specific optional history fields where semantically appropriate: use applicable menstruation/fertility artwork for menstrual, cervical, and fertility history and relevant ovulation artwork for known ovulation/fertility history or clinically/user-confirmed ovulation information, but do not use follicle-stage or ovulation artwork to ask users to guess internal biological events they could not reasonably know; predicted ovulation remains the responsibility of the Cycle Prediction Engine and must stay distinct from user-reported or clinically confirmed information. Pregnancy/fertilization artwork should remain in its existing educational/contextual systems unless a specific asset corresponds truthfully to information the user can report; never make the user supply biological details merely to achieve asset coverage. Every Personal Health Context category must support add, edit, remove, skip, and “prefer not to say” where appropriate, plus a general “anything else you want Fruitfolio to know?” field for information that fits nowhere else. All information entered here must be explicitly labeled and stored as user-provided context, remain distinct from calculated/predicted/AI-derived information, feed one shared health-context model available to Cycle Tracker and Ask where relevant, and be usable only to contextualize Research-Library-supported information—not to independently diagnose, establish causation, fabricate medical facts, or override the Research Library. The interface should use progressive disclosure so users explore whichever illustrated categories are relevant to them rather than being forced through every medical-history category during onboarding, and the complete Personal Health Context profile must remain reopenable and editable after onboarding with changes immediately propagated to applicable personalization and AI context.

PROMPT 1B ADDITION — EVIDENCE-INFORMED MY CONTEXT → CYCLE TRACKER ADAPTATION (2026-10-16; binding requirement). requirements.description: FRUIT BASKET — STAR / BAD-FRUIT MECHANIC: A standalone star functions as a single-use pass against the round-ending consequence of catching one BAD fruit. When the player successfully catches a star, store one available star pass. If the player subsequently catches a BAD fruit while a star pass is available, consume one star pass and allow the catch round to continue instead of ending it. If the player catches a BAD fruit without an available star pass, the catch round ends. A star therefore does not count as GOOD fruit toward filling the basket and does not independently complete the round; its gameplay purpose is specifically to protect the player from the next otherwise round-ending BAD-fruit catch. Stars must still be caught normally by fully entering the basket and receiving the same convincing flattened/settled catch treatment used for fruit.
evidence: Stackable pass consumption/final-state logic checked; catch penetration, flattened rendering, rarity, vines and full game UI still need acceptance.

requirements.description: FRUIT BASKET — STACKABLE STAR PASSES: Standalone stars are rare beneficial drops that the player can catch independently of fruit. There is no maximum number of stars the player may collect; every successfully caught star adds one star pass to the player’s currently available total. Star passes accumulate and remain available during the applicable catch round until consumed. If the player catches a BAD fruit while at least one star pass is available, automatically consume exactly one star pass and allow the round to continue. If the player catches a BAD fruit with zero star passes available, the round ends. GOOD fruit continues to count toward normal basket progress; standalone stars do not count as GOOD fruit or toward the basket-completion target. Stars should be genuinely rare drops, functioning as occasional earned protection rather than appearing frequently enough to remove the risk of BAD fruit. A star must fully enter the basket to count as caught and should visibly flatten/settle on impact using the same convincing catch treatment as fruit. Stars are also affected by vines and should visibly struggle/slow while passing through them.
evidence: Stackable pass consumption/final-state logic checked; catch penetration, flattened rendering, rarity, vines and full game UI still need acceptance.

requirements.description: FRUIT BASKET — VINES: Standalone stars are affected by vines just like GOOD fruit. When a star or GOOD fruit encounters the vine obstacle, it should visibly struggle/slow while passing through it, with the existing vine interaction/audio treatment. BAD fruit does not use this vine interaction. The animation and physics must make the resistance visually believable rather than merely reducing velocity invisibly.

FRUIT BASKET — PUDDLE: Basket inertia applies only while the basket is physically passing through the puddle. The basket’s movement/animation must visually communicate that it is actually moving through the puddle and encountering resistance rather than simply applying an unexplained slowdown. Once the basket has exited the puddle, normal basket movement resumes; the puddle must not leave an unintended persistent inertia effect.
